arxiv-1812-07244.title: Thermal gradient driven domain wall dynamics
arxiv-1812-07244.creator: M. T. Islam, X. S. Wang, X. R. Wang
arxiv-1812-07244.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by M. T. Islam, X. S. Wang, X. R. Wang. The issue of whether a thermal gradient acts like a magnetic field or an electric current in the domain wall (DW) dynamics is investigated. Broadly speaking, magnetization control knobs can be classified as energy-driving or angular-momentum driving forces.

arxiv-2110-03071.title: “Two Many Cooks”: Understanding Dynamic Human - Agent Team Communication and Perception Using Overcooked 2
arxiv-2110-03071.creator: Andres Rosero, Faustina Dinh, Ewart J. de Visser, Tyler Shaw, Elizabeth Phillips
arxiv-2110-03071.description: Abstract This paper describes a research study that aims to investigate changes in effective communication during human-AI collaboration with special attention to the perception of competence among team members and varying levels of task load placed on the team. We will also investigate differences between human-human teamwork and human-agent teamwork.

arxiv-2205-11910.title: Instability of oscillations in the Rosenzweig-MacArthur model of one consumer and two resources
arxiv-2205-11910.creator: Przemysław Gawroński, Alfio Borzì, Krzysztof Kułakowski
arxiv-2205-11910.description: Abstract The system of two resources R 1 R_{1} , R 2 R_{2} and one consumer C C is investigated within the Rosenzweig-MacArthur model with Holling type II functional response. The rates β i \beta_{i} of consumption of resources i = 1 , 2 i=1,2 are coupled by the condition β 1 + β 2 = 1 \beta_{1}+\beta_{2}=1 .

arxiv-2209-04295.title: 2D Weyl Materials in the Presence of Constant Magnetic Fields
arxiv-2209-04295.creator: Yaraslau Tamashevich, Leone Di Mauro Villari, Marco Ornigotti
arxiv-2209-04295.description: Abstract In this work we investigate the effect of a constant external, or artificial, magnetic field on the nonlinear response of 2D Weyl materials. We calculate the Landau Levels for tilted cones in 2D Weyl materials by treating the tilting in a perturbative manner, and employ perturbation theory to calculate the tilting-induced correction to the magnetic field induced Landau spectrum.

arxiv-2212-04545.title: The role of super-spreaders in modeling of SARS-CoV-2 Journal: Journal of Infectious Disease Modeling
arxiv-2212-04545.creator: François Rousse 1, Marcus Carlsson 2, Magnus Ögren 1,3,∗, Benjamin Kalischer Wellander 4
arxiv-2212-04545.description: Abstract In stochastic modeling of infectious diseases, it has been established that variations in infectivity affect the probability of a major outbreak, but not the shape of the curves during a major outbreak, which is predicted by deterministic models [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2302-09517.title: Transient photocurrent and optical absorption of disordered thin-film semiconductors: in-depth injection and nonlinear response
arxiv-2302-09517.creator: Kazuhiko Seki, Naoya Muramatsu, Tomoaki Miura, Tadaaki Ikoma
arxiv-2302-09517.description: Abstract The time-of-flight method is a fundamental approach for characterizing the transport properties of semiconductors. Recently, the transient photocurrent and optical absorption kinetics have been simultaneously measured for thin films; pulsed-light excitation of thin films should give rise to non-negligible in-depth carrier injection.

arxiv-2309-15339.title: Detecting quantum phase transitions in a frustrated spin chain via transfer learning of a quantum classifier algorithm
arxiv-2309-15339.creator: André J. Ferreira-Martins, Leandro Silva, Alberto Palhares, Rodrigo Pereira, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Rafael Chaves, Askery Canabarro
arxiv-2309-15339.description: Abstract The classification of phases and the detection of phase transitions are central and challenging tasks in diverse fields. Within physics, it relies on the identification of order parameters and the analysis of singularities in the free energy and its derivatives. Here, we propose an alternative framework to identify quantum phase transitions.

arxiv-2409-15394.title: Neural Control Variates with Automatic Integration
arxiv-2409-15394.creator: Zilu Li, Guandao Yang, Qingqing Zhao, Xi Deng, Leonidas Guibas, Bharath Hariharan, Gordon Wetzstein
arxiv-2409-15394.description: Abstract . This paper presents a method to leverage arbitrary neural network architecture for control variates. Control variates are crucial in reducing the variance of Monte Carlo integration, but they hinge on finding a function that both correlates with the integrand and has a known analytical integral.

arxiv-2503-16693.title: ATOM: A Framework of Detecting Query-Based Model Extraction Attacks for Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2503-16693.creator: Zhan Cheng, Bolin Shen, Tianming Sha, Yuan Gao, Shibo Li, Yushun Dong
arxiv-2503-16693.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhan Cheng, Bolin Shen, Tianming Sha, Yuan Gao, Shibo Li, Yushun Dong. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have gained traction in Graph-based Machine Learning as a Service (GMLaaS) platforms, yet they remain vulnerable to graph-based model extraction attacks (MEAs), where adversaries reconstruct surrogate models by querying the victim model. Existing defense mechanisms, such as watermarking and fingerprinting, suffer from poor real-time performance, susceptibility to evasion, or reliance on post-attack verification, making them inadequate for handling the dynamic characteristics of graph-based MEA variants.

arxiv-2601-02554.title: AI-exposed jobs deteriorated before ChatGPT
arxiv-2601-02554.creator: M. R. Frank, A. Javadian Sabet, L. Simon, S. H. Bana, R. Yu
arxiv-2601-02554.description: Abstract Public debate links worsening job prospects for AI-exposed occupations to the release of ChatGPT in late 2022. Using monthly U.S. unemployment insurance records, we measure occupation- and location-specific unemployment risk and find that risk rose in AI-exposed occupations beginning in early 2022, months before ChatGPT.

arxiv-2603-03076.creator: Jakob Hofstad

pmc-10670671.title: An Acid-Free Alternative to Pectin Production from the Cell Walls of Olive Oil Waste and Different Fruits Using Choline Chloride
pmc-10670671.creator: Alejandra Bermúdez-Oria, María Luisa Castejón, África Fernández-Prior, Guillermo Rodríguez-Gutiérrez, Juan Fernández-Bolaños, Bruno Medronho, María José Aliaño-González
pmc-10670671.description: The pectin from the cell walls of olive waste (alperujo) and apple, orange and strawberry fruits was extracted using choline chloride (ChCl) and the yield and chemical and structural compositions were compared to pectin extracted using citric acid (CA) and ammonium oxalate/oxalic acid (AOOA).

pmc-11427889.title: Bispecific FpFs: a versatile tool for preclinical antibody development†
pmc-11427889.creator: Matthew Collins, Nkiru Ibeanu, Wiktoria Roksana Grabowska, Sahar Awwad, Peng T. Khaw, Steve Brocchini, Hanieh Khalili
pmc-11427889.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We previously described FpFs 1̲ (Fab–PEG–Fab) as binding mimetics of IgGs. FpFs are prepared with di(bis-sulfone) conjugation reagents 3̲ that undergo disulfide rebridging conjugation with the accessible disulfide of each Fab (Scheme 1). We have now prepared bispecific FpFs 2̲ (bsFpF and Fab1–PEG–Fab2) as potential bispecific antibody mimetics with the intent that bsFpFs could be used in preclinical antibody development since sourcing bispecific antibodies may be challenging during preclinical research.

pmc-11494098.title: Local hydroclimate alters interpretation of speleothem δ18O records
pmc-11494098.creator: E W Patterson, V Skiba, A Wolf, M L Griffiths, D McGee, T N Bùi, M X Trần, T H Đinh, Q Đỗ-Trọng, G R Goldsmith, V Ersek, K R Johnson
pmc-11494098.description: Oxygen isotopes (δ18O) are the most commonly utilized speleothem proxy and have provided many foundational records of paleoclimate. Thus, understanding processes affecting speleothem δ18O is crucial. Yet, prior calcite precipitation (PCP), a process driven by local hydrology, is a widely ignored control of speleothem δ18O.

pmc-11672504.title: Presence of Borrelia Spirochetes in White Stork (Ciconia ciconia), White-Tailed Eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla), and Eastern Imperial Eagle (Aquila heliaca): Hospitalized in a Wild Bird Hospital and Sanctuary (Hortobágy, Hungary)
pmc-11672504.creator: András Pál Bózsik, János Déri, Béla Pál Bózsik, Borisz Egri, Paola Galluzzo, Guido Ruggero Loria, Sergio Migliore
pmc-11672504.description: Simple SummaryWild birds fly across countries and continents. They carry pathogens in their blood, and they might also carry infected parasites like ticks or lice. Their flight path spreads diseases over long distances. Some birds may carry pathogens that are not infectious to the birds themselves, only to humans, in which case they are reservoirs for these bacteria.

pmc-12969942.title: A Case of a Novel Perforin Gene Variant in Severe Familial Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Type 2 (FHL2)
pmc-12969942.creator: Hiroshi Yamauchi, Moeko Hino, Kazuyuki Meguro, Taiji Nakano, Takahiro Aoki, Yoshiharu Yamashita, Tomoko Okunushi, Takeshi Yamamoto, Hironori Sato, Takahiro Yasumi, Yuiko Hirata, Hirofumi Shibata, Hiroshi Nakajima, Hiromichi Hamada
pmc-12969942.description: IntroductionHemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life‐threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive cytokine release from activated T cells and macrophages. Primary HLH, or familial HLH (FHL), results from genetic mutations affecting cytotoxic lymphocyte function.Case ReportWe present a case of FHL Type 2 (FHL2) caused by compound heterozygous variants in the PRF1 gene, including one novel missense variant of p.Ala21Val (A21V).

pmc-13025100.title: Short-Term Heart Rate Variability Dynamics and Mortality Risk After Acute Coronary Syndrome
pmc-13025100.creator: Nikola Marković, Maša Petrović, Silvana Babić, Milovan Bojić, Branislav Milovanović
pmc-13025100.description: Background/Objectives: Heart rate variability (HRV) is a non-invasive marker of autonomic nervous system function with established prognostic value after acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The clinical relevance of temporal changes in short-term HRV remains insufficiently defined. This study evaluated short-term HRV dynamics and their association with mortality after ACS. Methods: This retrospective–prospective study included 230 patients with acute myocardial infarction.

pmc-13127303.title: Long-term risk of irritable bowel syndrome associated with triglyceride-glucose related indices: a large-scale prospective cohort study
pmc-13127303.creator: Haorui Liu, Si Liu, Qian Zhang, Shutian Zhang, Shengtao Zhu, Shanshan Wu
pmc-13127303.description: Background:Insulin resistance (IR) may play a crucial role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) pathogenesis. However, it remains unclear whether triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-related indices, useful biomarkers for assessing IR, are associated with IBS development.Objectives:To investigated the link between baseline TyG-related indices and incident IBS.Design:A prospective, population-based cohort study.

pmc-13239486.title: Effectiveness of sprint interval training in enhancing adolescent physical fitness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13239486.creator: Tiancheng Xu, Songpeng Su
pmc-13239486.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13384975.title: Gut microbiota profiles in reactive and metastatic lymphadenopathy in colorectal cancer: a tumor location–stratified analysis
pmc-13384975.creator: Toru Miyake, Masatsugu Kojima, Soichiro Tani, Keiji Muramoto, Hiromitsu Maehira, Sachiko Kaida, Tomoharu Shimizu, Masaji Tani
pmc-13384975.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposePreoperative lymphadenopathy in colorectal cancer may represent nodal metastasis or reactive change. We aimed to compare gut microbiota profiles between reactive and metastatic lymphadenopathy and to explore microbial features associated with nonmetastatic lymph node enlargement.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective observational study of colorectal cancer patients with radiological lymphadenopathy who underwent resection at Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital between 2018 and 2021. For the primary analysis, we included patients with radiological lymphadenopathy on preoperative CT.

pmc-13536820.title: The role of classical protein tyrosine phosphatases in diabetic kidney disease and therapeutic implications
pmc-13536820.creator: Grace LeBleu, Fawaz G Haj
pmc-13536820.description: Approximately one-third of people with diabetes have diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and DKD remains a leading cause of kidney failure in the United States. DKD is characterized by injury to the glomerular filtration barrier and renal tubulointerstitium, arising from complex and convergent metabolic, hemodynamic, and inflammatory insults.

pmc-13662248.title: Association of Intraoperative Ketorolac Administration with Pediatric Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13662248.creator: Muaaz Wajahath, Ahmad Hassan, Amir Mahdi Ghafarian, Malik Al-Jamal, Abdul-Lateef Shafu, Haytham Al-Qasmi, Walid Yasir
pmc-13662248.description: BackgroundPediatric anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is increasingly common. Optimizing pain management while minimizing opioid exposure is a priority. Intraoperative ketorolac, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), is used for analgesia, but its impact on healing and surgical outcomes remains controversial. This study evaluates the effects of intraoperative ketorolac on postoperative outcomes in pediatric ACLR patients (< 18 years).
